message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "validate_mediastinal_shift_direction", "description": "When interpreting chest imaging with significant unilateral opacity, explicitly verify the direction of mediastinal shift to distinguish between space-occupying lesions (e.g., effusion) and volume-loss conditions (e.g., atelectasis).", "applicable_conditions": "Any task involving the interpretation of chest X-rays or CT scans where a large unilateral opacity, consolidation, or pleural abnormality is detected.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": ["chest_xray_report_generator", "chest_xray_classifier"], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "If a large unilateral opacity is identified: (1) Use `chest_xray_report_generator` to specifically extract descriptions of mediastinal position (trachea, heart border); (2) Cross-reference this with `chest_xray_classifier` findings for effusion vs. collapse/atelectasis probabilities; (3) Apply the rule: Contralateral shift suggests space-occupying pathology (e.g., massive effusion), while Ipsilateral shift suggests volume loss (e.g., atelectasis/collapse). Do not assume shift direction based on opacity alone; confirm via explicit report extraction."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
